summary: Backend validation of the 11 newly-injected features (PIN auth, void sale, kasir history, bank accounts, QRIS/setting KV, outlet strict isolation, shift lock, cash opname variance, vendor scope, security headers + CSRF). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iteration10_new_features.py with 25 tests across 10 test classes. Initial run surfaced (a) kasir demo password had been rotated to '1234' on the live DB (blocking most Kasir tests) — restored to MjdKupi#2026 via /api/admin/users/{id}/reset-password, and (b) a real backend persistence bug in POST /api/settings/bank-accounts (JSON column mutation not committed to Postgres — SQLAlchemy dirty tracking missed the reassignment because the accounts list was aliased from row.value before reassignment). Fixed by (i) copying the list with list(...) instead of aliasing and (ii) calling sqlalchemy.orm.attributes.flag_modified(row, 'value') on both POST and DELETE. Also aligned endpoint paths — review request mentioned /api/pos/pin/*, /api/pos/void, /api/shift/history but actual server endpoints are /api/admin/pin/generate, /api/sales/{id}/void, /api/pos/history, /api/shifts/{open,close} (plural). Final result: 25/25 PASSED.

minor.issue: FIXED — SQLAlchemy JSON column mutations were not being persisted because the accounts list was aliased from row.value.get('accounts') and mutated in place before reassignment, so SA's change detection saw equal values. Now uses list(...) copy + flag_modified().

Kasir password on live Supabase was '1234' (rotated by a previous frontend admin test). Reset to MjdKupi#2026 to match /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Seed logic only rotates the superadmin password — other demo users are not re-synced on startup.

Path differs from review-request spec (/api/pos/pin/generate). No /api/pos/pin/verify endpoint exists — verification is done inline inside /api/sales/{id}/void via internal _verify_pin(). PIN alphabet is alphanumeric (32-char), not strictly numeric — 6-character token, not 6-digit as spec says. Consider aligning spec vs impl.
generate_pin is gated to 'Super Admin' AND 'Admin' — review request said 'Super Admin only'. Not blocking, just flag scope broader than spec.

action_items: Confirm main agent is OK with fix applied to POST/DELETE /api/settings/bank-accounts (flag_modified on JSON column). Consider a systematic sweep for other JSON columns that mutate in place (Setting.value updates in PIN generate, QRIS save, generic upsert appear safe because they build fresh dicts, but any future in-place list/dict mutation on a JSON column must call flag_modified()).
Reconcile endpoint paths — either add aliases /api/pos/pin/generate, /api/pos/void, /api/shift/history so review-request URLs work, or update product/spec docs to use the actual paths.
Add /api/pos/pin/verify endpoint if PIN verification needs to be exposed to the frontend (currently only usable indirectly through void sale).
Make the seeder re-sync demo user passwords (currently only superadmin gets rotated). Otherwise QA env credentials drift silently after any admin-panel password change.
critical_code_review_comments: SQLAlchemy JSON column mutation pattern is fragile — the codebase has ~6 sites that read row.value, mutate/re-wrap, and reassign. Only bank-accounts hit the aliasing trap because it explicitly does row.value.get('accounts', []) which returns the internal list. Recommend either (a) wrap Setting.value with MutableDict.as_mutable(JSON) in models.py, or (b) standardize on flag_modified() after every JSON reassignment.
generate_pin stores the PIN in cleartext inside mjd_settings — acceptable for a 15-minute authorization code (not a password), but note it in the security review.

Void sale allows Kasir to void OTHER kasirs' sales as long as they hold a valid PIN because the ownership check is only enforced when user.role == 'Kasir' and sale.cashier_id != user.id — that DOES restrict it. Good.
Shift close does not scope M.Sale.status != 'voided' to sale.outlet_id == shift.outlet_id — relies on shift_id linkage. OK because sales carry shift_id.

Kitchen tickets are created with outlet_id from the sale — good. But create_kitchen_tickets does another commit inside the sale flow, resulting in two commits per sale (sale commit + kitchen commit). Consider batching.
list_products anonymous branch is fine but current_user is called with request=None; the code guards it, but any future refactor could crash. Minor robustness concern.
Kasir /api/sales GET returns [] silently when no active shift — frontend may render blank. Consider surfacing a hint via headers or an empty-state flag.

rca of the issue: Bug: POST /api/settings/bank-accounts returned 200 with the new list but subsequent GET returned {"accounts":[]}. Root cause: SQLAlchemy JSON columns without MutableDict don't track in-place mutations. The handler did `accounts = row.value.get('accounts', [])` which aliased the internal list, then `accounts.append(...)` mutated it in place (silently modifying row.value too), then `row.value = {'accounts': accounts}`. When SA compared previous and new attribute values for change detection, both dicts referenced the same mutated list — no dirty flag set → the UPDATE was never emitted (or was optimized away). Fix: `accounts = list(row.value.get('accounts', []) or [])` to break the alias + `flag_modified(row, 'value')` to force SA to emit UPDATE. Verified via curl POST→GET and via pytest TestBankAccounts.test_crud_roundtrip.
